subject: biology
title: Exchange surfaces and surface area to volume ratio
key_idea: Cells need to take in substances such as oxygen and get rid of waste. Small organisms can do this across their surface. Large organisms have a small **surface area to volume ratio**, so they need exchange surfaces with a large surface area and a transport system.

sections.heading: Why large organisms need exchange surfaces

blocks.text: Every cell must take in substances and remove waste. Substances move into and out of cells by diffusion. **Diffusion** is the net movement of particles from where they are in high concentration to where they are in low concentration.

A single-celled organism is very small. It has a large surface area compared with its volume. Substances have only a short distance to travel to reach the middle of the cell, so diffusion across the cell surface is enough.

A large organism is different. As an organism gets bigger, its volume increases faster than its surface area. This means it has a smaller surface area to volume ratio. The distance from the surface to the middle is also much greater. Diffusion alone would take too long to supply the cells deep inside.

Large multicellular organisms solve this in two ways. They have specialised **exchange surfaces**, which are parts of the body where substances cross in and out. They also have a **transport system**, such as the blood, which carries substances between the exchange surface and the cells.

sections.heading: Calculating surface area to volume ratio

blocks.text: The **surface area to volume ratio** is the surface area divided by the volume. It is written as a ratio such as 6 : 1, which means 6 units of surface area for every 1 unit of volume.

For a cube, the surface area is 6 × side × side, because a cube has six square faces. The volume is side × side × side. A cube with sides of 2 cm has a surface area of 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 cm² and a volume of 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cm³. The ratio is 24 : 8, which is 3 : 1.

For a block that is not a cube, work out the area of each face, add them to get the total surface area, then divide by the volume. For a block with sides X, Y and Z, the surface area is 2XY + 2XZ + 2YZ.

diagram.alt: A line graph showing the surface area to volume ratio of a cube falling steeply as the side of the cube increases from 1 cm to 6 cm, then falling more slowly.

blocks.text: As size increases, the surface area to volume ratio decreases. The same pattern holds for animals. A small animal has a large ratio and a large animal has a small ratio.
Organisms take in some substances and get rid of others. The table shows the ones you need to know.

rows: Needed by all cells. Plants take it in from the soil
Dissolved food molecules, such as glucose
Needed for healthy growth. Plants take them in from the soil
A waste product made when excess amino acids are broken down. It is carried in the blood to the kidneys and removed in urine

blocks.text: Exchange surfaces are adapted so that diffusion is fast. The alveoli in the lungs, the gills of a fish and the villi in the small intestine are all examples.

items: A **large surface area**, for example from folds or many small projections, so that more particles can cross at once.
**Thin walls**, often one cell thick, so that the diffusion distance is short.
A **good blood supply**, or a network of capillaries, which carries substances away and keeps a steep concentration gradient.
Ventilation in the lungs and gills, which keeps a steep concentration gradient by bringing fresh air or water to the surface.

blocks.text: A steep concentration gradient means a big difference in concentration between the two sides of the surface. The steeper it is, the faster the diffusion.

sections.heading: Investigating the effect of surface area to volume ratio

blocks.text: A common investigation uses jelly cubes of different sizes. The jelly contains an indicator that changes colour when acid reaches it. The cubes are placed in acid, and the time for the colour to change throughout each cube is measured.

Small cubes change colour faster. They have a larger surface area to volume ratio, so acid diffuses to the middle more quickly. The conclusion is that a higher surface area to volume ratio gives a faster rate of diffusion.
The rate of colour change is 1 ÷ time. A cube that takes 132 seconds has a rate of 1 ÷ 132 = 0.0076, which is 7.6 × 10⁻³ per second in standard form.

checks.q: Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of a cube with sides of 3 cm.
checks.a: Surface area = 6 × 3 × 3 = 54 cm². Volume = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cm³. Ratio = 54 : 27 = 2 : 1.

checks.q: Explain why a large multicellular organism needs a transport system but a single-celled organism does not.
checks.a: A large organism has a small surface area to volume ratio and a long diffusion distance, so diffusion alone would take too long. A single-celled organism has a large ratio and a short distance, so diffusion is enough.

checks.q: Give three ways an exchange surface is adapted for fast diffusion.
checks.a: A large surface area, thin walls (a short diffusion distance) and a good blood supply to keep a steep concentration gradient.

mistakes.wrong: The walls of the capillaries are thin cell walls.
mistakes.right: "Cell walls" is not accepted. Write that the walls are thin, or one cell thick, for a short diffusion distance.

mistakes.wrong: Arteries and veins give the gills a good blood supply.
mistakes.right: Arteries and veins are not accepted for capillaries. Write capillaries, or blood vessels.

mistakes.wrong: Alveoli have a steep concentration gradient.
mistakes.right: This is ignored on its own. Say that a good blood supply, or a capillary network, maintains the concentration gradient.

mistakes.wrong: A large animal needs a respiratory system because its surface area is too small.
mistakes.right: Say that it has a smaller surface area to volume ratio, so the diffusion distance is too large or diffusion takes too long.

worked_example.question:
Fish exchange gases through gills. Oxygen from the water enters the blood of a fish through the gills, which have filaments and capillaries.

Explain how gills are adapted to maximise the exchange of oxygen between the water and the blood.
answer_points: The gills and filaments provide a large surface area for diffusion.
A good blood supply, or a network of capillaries, maintains the concentration gradient.
The filaments and capillaries have thin walls, one cell thick, for a short diffusion distance.
The water is in close proximity to the blood supply for a short diffusion distance.
worked_example.tip: Each adaptation scores a mark only when it is linked to its effect on diffusion.

extra.heading: Surface area to volume ratio and heat loss (Higher tier)

blocks.text: A warm-blooded animal with a large surface area to volume ratio loses heat faster per unit volume. It needs a greater rate of respiration to release more heat and keep warm. Respiration is a large part of metabolism, so its metabolic rate is higher. Small warm-blooded animals therefore have a higher metabolic rate than large ones.

mistakes.right: "Cell walls" is rejected. Write that the walls or membranes are thin or one cell thick.

mistakes.wrong: The total surface area of a human lung is 70.
mistakes.right: A unit is needed to get the second mark: 70 m².

mistakes.wrong: Oxygen moves from the alveolus into the capillary by osmosis or active transport.
mistakes.right: Oxygen moves by diffusion. Osmosis is the movement of water, and diffusion needs no energy.

worked_example.question: Explain, using Fick's law, the factors that affect the diffusion rate of molecules into and out of cells.
answer_points: Fick's law: the rate of diffusion is proportional to surface area and concentration difference, and inversely proportional to the thickness of the membrane.
Surface area: as surface area increases, the rate of diffusion increases, because there are more places for diffusion to happen.
Concentration difference: the larger the difference between inside and outside the cell, the faster the rate of diffusion.
Thickness of the membrane: the thicker the membrane, the slower the rate of diffusion, because the diffusion distance is greater.
worked_example.tip: Full marks need all three factors with their effects, and one reference to proportionality.

blocks.text: Fick's law links the rate of diffusion to three factors. The rate of diffusion is proportional to (surface area × concentration difference) ÷ thickness of the membrane.

rows: More places for particles to cross

mistakes.wrong: Surface area to volume ratio and rate of diffusion are directly proportional.
mistakes.right: "Directly proportional" is ignored. Write that a higher surface area to volume ratio gives a faster rate of diffusion, or that there is a positive correlation.

mistakes.wrong: In emphysema, oxygen cannot diffuse into the blood.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Write that the surface area of the alveoli is reduced, so diffusion of oxygen is reduced or harder.

mistakes.wrong: The eggshell lets gases in and out so the chick can breathe.
mistakes.right: "Gases in and out" and "breathing" are ignored. Write that oxygen reaches the chick, carbon dioxide escapes, and the chick can respire.

worked_example.question:
Some students investigate the effect of the surface area : volume ratio on the rate of diffusion in animal cells.

They use hydrochloric acid and gelatine cubes that have been stained blue using a pH indicator solution. The indicator will turn red in acidic conditions.

They put different sized cubes into 3 different test tubes of hydrochloric acid and time how long it takes for the cubes to completely change to red.

The table shows the students' results.

Length of each side of the cube (mm) | surface area : volume ratio | Time to completely change colour (seconds)
2 | | 32
4 | 3 : 2 | 61
6 | 1 : 1 | 170

Calculate the surface area : volume ratio for the cube with sides of 2 mm.
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 3 : 1 on the answer line scores both marks. Show 24 : 8 to be safe.
